definition: P31 constituency-level and P32 ward-level evidence-state closures for the three maize indicators (IND-MAIZE-AREA, IND-MAIZE-PRODUCTION, IND-MAIZE-YIELD). These three indicators carry no county, constituency or ward slot in the P18 public-taxonomy (data/indicators/seed/placeholder-taxonomy.json mentions them only in passing, in a note on an unrelated retired indicator) -- they surface only through the raw canonical indicator registry and the P26-P30 local-54 framework -- so a genuinely researched, specifically-cited closure for them cannot live in the shared data/completeness/evidence-states.json without risking that file's P18-specific, exact-count reconciliation (scripts/completeness/validate-slot-ledger.mjs) or a merge conflict with other P31/P32 batches concurrently adding their own entries there. This file is consumed only by scripts/p29/build-local-54-slot-ledger.mjs, exactly like data/completeness/evidence-states.json, but scoped to indicators/levels the older P18 taxonomy never covered. It never manufactures a zero, proxy, regional inheritance or synthetic observation -- every entry is a governed official_unavailable closure with a specific, checkable, cited investigation. The P32 ward-level entries (2026-09-19) are not a mechanical extension of the P31 constituency entries (2026-09-18): each re-ran the KilimoSTAT and opendata.go.ke platform checks live and added a fresh ward-specific check of five major maize-growing counties' own government publications before closing.

states.period_label: 2023 Annex 1 maize-by-county tabulation, county-only -- no constituency-level publication exists
states.source: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, National Agriculture Production Report (2023 edition, Annex 1: '2023 Maize by County') -- the same source this Atlas already cites at county level for these three indicators
states.reason: P31 conducted a genuine, multi-source investigation into constituency-level maize statistics before closing this maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell, rather than assuming unavailability or spatially allocating the county figure. Findings, each independently checked on 2026-09-18: (1) KNBS's National Agriculture Production Report -- the 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions were each located and inspected; county is the finest geographic tier tabulated for maize area, production and yield in every edition, with no sub-county, constituency or ward table in any of them. (2) KilimoSTAT (statistics.kilimo.go.ke), the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development's own agricultural open-data platform, is not usable in practice: its HTTPS endpoint fails with an expired TLS certificate, blocking both direct navigation and this project's fetch tooling; a 2024-05-30 Internet Archive capture of its own published 'List of Publications' page (retrieved because the live site could not be) lists no maize or crop-production sub-county dataset among its titles -- only county/national-level compendia (e.g. the KIPPRA Agricultural Sector Data Compendium) and unrelated policy documents. (3) opendata.go.ke, the national open-data portal (an ArcGIS Hub deployment), could not be used for dataset discovery: its machine-readable catalogue (data.json) returns the error "SB_0006: Subscription is canceled, the item is not accessible" for the entire portal, and a previously search-indexed 'Kisumu County Crop Statistics' dataset -- whose own search snippet described sub-county-level projected and actual crop yields -- is now a dead link both on the live site and in every Wayback Machine capture checked; this independently reproduces this project's prior finding that opendata.go.ke's dataset-search API is unreachable (HTTP 401/subscription-canceled) for a different P31 batch's indicators. (4) HarvestStat Africa (Nature Scientific Data, 2025; the largest open-access harmonized compilation of official subnational crop statistics for Sub-Saharan Africa, built from FEWS NET/USAID-collated national reporting) explicitly documents Kenya as covered only at Admin-1 (county) level -- unlike 15 other African countries (Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Malawi, Zambia and others) that it covers down to Admin-2. This is strong independent evidence that no official Kenyan sub-county maize compilation has ever entered even the most comprehensive pan-African harmonization effort. (5) A peer-reviewed sub-county maize-yield study (Simbolon et al., Scientific Reports 2024, PMC11190209) confirms that the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development (MoALD) does hold genuine administrative sub-county maize-yield records for Trans Nzoia and Uasin Gishu Counties covering 2017-2021 -- the paper explicitly thanks MoALD 'for providing yield data for validation within the ADM project' -- but that underlying sub-county table was shared privately with the named research team for model validation and was never itself published; the paper's own Data Availability statement lists only its remote-sensing and crop-model inputs (FAO WaPOR, DSSAT-CERES-Maize parameters), not the MoALD administrative table, so it cannot be cited as a public source here. (6) Kenya's first-ever Census of Agriculture (2025/26 KCA, per KNBS's own framing that 'Kenya has never conducted a comprehensive census of agriculture since independence') is explicitly intended to eventually 'provide a complete structural picture of agricultural holdings disaggregated to lower administrative units', but as of this review has published only a 2024/25 pilot survey report; its main national results are not yet released. (7) A news report (Capital FM/capitalfm.africa, January 2026) citing sub-county 2024 maize tonnage for Ainabkoi, Moiben and Turbo Sub-Counties in Uasin Gishu, attributed only to 'the Uasin Gishu County Government, compiled in collaboration with KNBS' with no named or dated report, was checked and rejected as a source: it names no citable publication, and its own figures are internally inconsistent with the county total this Atlas already publishes (crediting Ainabkoi alone with roughly three-quarters of the entire county's reported maize tonnage), so it does not meet this project's standard for a defensible official citation. No publicly checkable, citable, internally-consistent source therefore reports maize statistics below county level today. Per this project's anti-fabrication rule, the county 2023 Annex 1 figure is never spatially allocated down into the 290 constituency rows; this maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell is closed as official_unavailable pending either the KCA's main release or a future MoALD publication of its confirmed-to-exist sub-county administrative records.
states.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes the main 2025/26 Kenya Census of Agriculture results disaggregated below county, or MoALD/KilimoSTAT publicly releases the sub-county administrative maize records confirmed to exist (per Simbolon et al. 2024) for at least Trans Nzoia and Uasin Gishu Counties, or a future National Agriculture Production Report edition adds a constituency/sub-county annex.

states.period_label: 2023 Annex 1 maize-by-county tabulation, county-only -- no constituency- or ward-level publication exists
states.source: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, National Agriculture Production Report (2023 edition, Annex 1: '2023 Maize by County') -- the same source this Atlas already cites at county level for these three indicators; ward-level absence independently re-confirmed 2026-09-19 against KilimoSTAT (statistics.kilimo.go.ke, expired TLS certificate) and opendata.go.ke (host unreachable) and against the published agriculture-department materials of Uasin Gishu, Trans Nzoia, Bungoma, Nakuru and Nandi County Governments
states.reason: P32 conducted a genuine, fresh ward-level re-investigation on 2026-09-19 before closing this maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell, rather than mechanically copying the P31 constituency closure. A ward is strictly finer than a constituency (each of the 290 constituencies subdivides into its own wards), so the P31 constituency-level finding (contract P31-AGRICULTURE-MAIZE-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE-2026-09-18-IND-MAIZE-AREA, same file) applies a fortiori: KNBS's National Agriculture Production Report (2023, 2024 and 2025 editions) tabulates maize area, production and yield no finer than county, so no constituency-level table exists from which a ward table could in turn be derived. Because administrative (non-survey) data collection in principle could exist at finer resolution than a fixed survey design, this closure did not simply extend the constituency finding -- it re-ran the two national platform checks and added a new, ward-specific check across Kenya's five largest maize-growing counties, as follows. (1) KilimoSTAT (statistics.kilimo.go.ke), MoALD's own agricultural open-data platform, was re-tested live on 2026-09-19: its HTTPS endpoint still fails outright with an expired TLS certificate (curl/schannel error SEC_E_CERT_EXPIRED, "The received certificate has expired"), identical to the P31 finding a day earlier -- the certificate has not been renewed and the platform remains unusable for dataset discovery. (2) opendata.go.ke, the national ArcGIS Hub open-data portal, was also re-tested live on 2026-09-19 and is now in a *worse* state than at P31 time: rather than returning the "SB_0006: Subscription is canceled" API error P31 documented, the entire host (opendata.go.ke, resolving to 169.239.252.108) no longer completes a TCP/TLS handshake at all -- both a direct HTTPS request and a fetch of its machine-readable data.json catalogue time out or are refused, confirming the portal provides no path to any dataset, ward-level or otherwise. (3) A new, ward-specific check was run for the five counties with the largest maize acreage nationally -- Uasin Gishu, Trans Nzoia, Bungoma, Nakuru and Nandi -- searching each county government's own agriculture-department pages, budget/ADP documents and local news coverage for any genuine, citable, official ward-level maize area/production/yield publication (as distinct from constituency/sub-county). None was found for any of the five counties. What did surface: county agriculture-department communications describing ward-level *input-distribution activity* (e.g. Nandi County's NAAIAP fertiliser distribution to Songhor/Soba ward in Tinderet Sub-County; Bungoma's seed/fertiliser subsidy counts reported by ward for 43 rural wards and 2 urban wards) -- these are extension-programme administrative records of farmer counts and input quantities, not maize area/production/yield statistics, and do not constitute a citable source for these indicators at any geography. The Capital Business/Capital FM article on Uasin Gishu maize value (republished January 2026 at capitalfm.co.ke, the same outlet P31 already investigated as capitalfm.africa) resurfaced in this fresh search reporting only sub-county (Ainabkoi, Moiben, Turbo), not ward-level, tonnage, attributed to no named or dated report; it was re-confirmed uncitable for the same reasons P31 documented (no citable underlying report; its Ainabkoi figure is internally inconsistent with the county total this Atlas already publishes). A third-party encyclopedia page (agriculture.co.ke) citing Bungoma sub-county (not ward) yield-per-acre figures was also checked and rejected: it names no official government report, and the specific page identified is itself no longer reachable (HTTP 404) on re-check. No county agriculture department among the five checked, and no national platform, publishes a citable official ward-level maize area, production or yield figure today. Per this project's anti-fabrication rule, the county-level 2023 Annex 1 KNBS figure is never spatially allocated down into ward rows, and no constituency-level figure (none exists) could be either. This maize area (hectares planted/harvested) cell is closed as official_unavailable for all 1,450 wards pending either KNBS's main 2025/26 Kenya Census of Agriculture release disaggregated below county, a future KilimoSTAT publication once its platform is restored, or a county government publishing its own ward-level administrative agriculture statistics (none currently does, per this check).
states.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes the main 2025/26 Kenya Census of Agriculture results disaggregated below county, or MoALD/KilimoSTAT publicly releases sub-county/ward administrative maize records once the KilimoSTAT platform is restored (its TLS certificate remains expired as of 2026-09-19), or any Kenyan county government publishes its own ward-level maize area/production/yield statistics (none of Uasin Gishu, Trans Nzoia, Bungoma, Nakuru or Nandi did so as of this 2026-09-19 check), or a future National Agriculture Production Report edition adds a constituency/ward annex.
